nodes.label: Cook-Torrance BRDF
nodes.rationale: Microfacet specular BRDF: specular = D*F*G/(4*NdotV*NdotL) where D is the GGX/Trowbridge-Reitz normal distribution (D_GGX), G is the Schlick-Smith geometric shadowing term (G_SchlicksmithGGX), and F is the Schlick Fresnel approximation (F_Schlick) with F0 mixed from 0.04 toward material color by metallic.

nodes.label: Physically Based Rendering (PBR)
nodes.rationale: Metallic-roughness PBR workflow sampling albedo/metallic/roughness/AO texture arrays; Lambertian diffuse (kD*albedo/PI) plus GGX Cook-Torrance specular; energy conservation via kD = (1-kS)*(1-metallic); sRGB decode (pow 2.2) on albedo, Reinhard tone mapping color/(color+1) and gamma encode on output.

nodes.label: Tangent-Space Normal Mapping
nodes.rationale: Builds a TBN matrix from interpolated normal, tangent and bitangent (B = cross(N,T)*tangentW), samples the normal map, remaps from [0,1] to [-1,1] and transforms the tangent-space normal into world space.

nodes.label: Shadow Mapping
nodes.rationale: Depth is rendered from the light's point of view (light-space MVP) into a shadow map; lit shaders project fragments into light space (shadowPos), compare stored depth against fragment depth with a slope-scaled bias to decide occlusion.

nodes.label: Percentage-Closer Filtering (PCF)
nodes.rationale: Softens shadow edges by sampling the shadow map over a 3x3 texel neighborhood (offset by texelSize) and averaging the 9 depth comparisons into a notInShadow factor.

nodes.label: GPU Skeletal Skinning
nodes.rationale: Vertex positions and normals are transformed by a linear blend of up to four joint matrices selected by inJointIndex and weighted by inJointWeight, accumulating gl_Position/fragPos/fragNorm for animated skinned meshes.

nodes.label: Skybox Rendering
nodes.rationale: Renders an environment background: vertex position used as direction, gl_Position set to pos.xyww so depth is forced to 1.0 (far plane); fragment converts the direction to spherical yaw/pitch UVs to sample an equirectangular skybox (and stars) texture.

nodes.label: Text Rendering
nodes.rationale: Draws screen-space glyph quads; the font atlas channels (R/G/B) act as masks combined via push-constant foreground, background and shadow colors to composite the final text pixel.

nodes.label: Collider Debug Visualization
nodes.rationale: Debug wireframe/overlay pass: transforms collider geometry by a view-projection matrix and colors it with a per-collider stroke color indexed by a push-constant colliderIndex, passing a flat color straight to the fragment output.

nodes.label: Shadow Map Visualization (debug view)
nodes.rationale: Debug view that draws the depth texture onto a full-screen triangle (UVs synthesized from gl_VertexIndex, scaled by a debug uniform) to inspect the contents of the shadow map.

nodes.label: Model Building (scene geometry setup)
nodes.source_file: E05 - Build the models~E05 - Build the models/shaders/SimplePos.vert.txt
nodes.rationale: E05 theme - assembling and rendering scene models: binding geometry with model / view-projection / normal matrices and feeding fragment position, UVs and light-space shadowPos into the lighting and shadow passes.

nodes.label: Motion / Skeletal Skinning
nodes.rationale: E06 theme - linear-blend skeletal skinning: each vertex carries 4 joint indices and weights that blend arrays of 65 bone matrices (mvpMat/mMat/nMat) to deform and animate characters.

nodes.label: Why TBN advanced texturing: build a TBN matrix from interpolated normal+tangent (fragTan.w handedness) to decode tangent-space normal maps, sample albedo/metallic/roughness/AO PBR maps, evaluate Cook-Torrance (GGX D, Smith G, Fresnel-Schlick F) with hemispheric ambient, then Reinhard tone-map + gamma.

nodes.label: Camera input handling (Starter.hpp)
nodes.rationale: Input is hardcoded in Starter.hpp: WASD movement, arrow keys for yaw/pitch, mouse only with left button held; cannot be changed without editing Starter (forbidden) or reimplementing (risky vs prof version).

nodes.label: Optional camera gravity
nodes.rationale: Gravity handled in the camera and made optional so disabling it enables a fly cheat/debug option.

nodes.label: Jump (spacebar impulse)
nodes.rationale: Bound to spacebar which Starter.hpp already wires to getSixAxis 'fire'; a simple upward velocity impulse gated behind its own optional flag, triggering only on fresh key press while grounded.

nodes.label: Grounded detection vs colliders
nodes.rationale: Cannot infer grounded from vertical velocity==0 because looking up/down while walking bleeds the front vector into vertical movement; ground contact is computed directly against colliders every frame.

nodes.label: Sprint (Ctrl)
nodes.rationale: Bound to Ctrl, not wired by Starter.hpp so polled directly via glfwGetKey, gated behind its own flag; can only start while grounded but releasing Ctrl stops it instantly even mid-air since movement is not persisted velocity (no momentum).

nodes.label: AABB floor collider
nodes.rationale: AABB-based ground detection provided by Colliders.hpp and Scene.hpp; declaring "collider":"AABB" in scene.json applies ground detection to whatever model is the floor.

nodes.label: Optional collision (no-clip cheat)
nodes.rationale: Collision detection is optional, controlled by a flag, enabling a no-clip cheat/debug option.

nodes.label: CheatFlags struct
nodes.rationale: gravityEnabled, collisionEnabled, jumpEnabled, sprintEnabled grouped into one CheatFlags struct (single 'cheats' member) instead of loose booleans; easy to find/reset as a block and a natural hook for a future debug UI. Call sites read through the struct e.g. if(cheats.gravityEnabled).

nodes.label: MovementParams struct
nodes.rationale: Numeric tuning (moveSpeed, sprintMultiplier, jumpSpeed, gravity) lives in a separate MovementParams struct because 'how strong' is a different concern than the CheatFlags 'on/off' bools, though both sit next to each other and share the no-persistence pattern.

nodes.label: No-persistence cheat defaults
nodes.rationale: CheatFlags is a plain struct with default member initializers, so it resets to legit defaults (all true = cheats off) every launch; no config file or serialization by design.

nodes.label: Deadline: last call February 2027
nodes.rationale: No fixed deadline, but the whole process must be completed before the last call in February 2027; presentations are scheduled near officially proposed exam dates.

nodes.label: Two-part presentation
nodes.rationale: Presentation = a 10-minute (hard cap) live demo of the application describing its challenges and extents, followed by individual questions where each member describes a specific part of the project.

nodes.label: All team members must be present
nodes.rationale: Projects are discussed by all members in the same session; every group component must be present for the presentation.
nodes.norm_label: all team members must be present

nodes.label: Project worth max 25 points
nodes.rationale: The project itself determines a maximum total of 25 points in the final evaluation.

nodes.label: Individual questions worth up to 8 points
nodes.rationale: Quality of answers to individual questions about a particular part of the code determines up to 8 points.
nodes.norm_label: individual questions worth up to 8 points

nodes.label: Each student must know the code in detail
nodes.rationale: Each student must know exactly and in great detail how their code works regardless of elapsed time; 'we did it long ago and don't remember' scores zero for that question.
nodes.norm_label: each student must know the code in detail

nodes.label: Source code upload, compile and inspection
nodes.rationale: Students upload the source code; it is compiled and checked to work as shown in the presentation, and part of the grade is based on analysis of the delivered source.
nodes.norm_label: source code upload, compile and inspection

nodes.label: Servizi Online exam registration
nodes.rationale: Students must always register via the online services page (plus project form) so the mark can be filled on the University server; the shown day/room is only one possible presentation day.

nodes.label: Final mark = project + questions (+ laude)
nodes.rationale: Final mark is the sum of project and question scores, with laude in special cases, communicated at end of session since code evaluation happens after presentations.

nodes.label: Plagiarism forces a new project
nodes.rationale: If there is clear evidence the project was not done directly by the students, they must do a new one to pass.

nodes.label: Score rejection and retrial rules
nodes.rationale: Students may reject the mark and retry (one try per session); retriers must improve/re-discuss; members individually accept or reject, and accepters are 'removed' from the group leaving others to improve alone.

nodes.label: Teams of two or three students
nodes.rationale: Projects must be done in teams of 2-3; individual projects only under special circumstances with motivation, groups of four only if pre-agreed with professors; all members discuss on the same exam date.
nodes.norm_label: teams of two or three students

nodes.label: C++ + Vulkan + Starter.hpp mandatory
nodes.rationale: Each project must be written in C++ using Vulkan and the course Starter.hpp.

nodes.label: Shaders must be written by yourself
nodes.rationale: Code must explicitly set the shaders, which must be written by the students themselves.
nodes.norm_label: shaders must be written by yourself

nodes.label: AI tools only for minor contribution
nodes.rationale: AI-based tools are allowed only if they give a minor contribution and the students fully understand EVERYTHING the tool created.
nodes.norm_label: ai tools only for minor contribution

nodes.label: Helper libraries must be open source
nodes.rationale: Any helper library not relevant to 3D graphics (physics, collisions, AI) is allowed, but must be easily found/installed online, open source, and included with the delivery so it compiles.
nodes.norm_label: helper libraries must be open source

nodes.label: Explicit Vulkan pipeline requirements
nodes.rationale: Code must have explicit sections that load/create geometries and textures, set shaders, define vertex formats and uniform blocks, create graphics pipelines and render passes, allocate command buffers, and record draw-calls.

nodes.label: Local/view/projection transform chain
nodes.rationale: Objects defined in local coordinates must pass through a local transform, then a view transform, then a projection to normalized screen coordinates.

nodes.label: World/view/projection matrix options
nodes.rationale: World matrices combine translation/rotation/scale (Euler or quaternion); view via look-at or look-in-direction; projection parallel or perspective, with the user able to view the scene from different points.

nodes.label: Meshes and multiple vertex formats
nodes.rationale: Objects are meshes with position, normals, texture coords and maybe tangent; loaded from OBJ/GLTF or generated procedurally; multiple vertex formats may coexist to reduce memory to needed attributes.

nodes.label: First/third person navigation controls
nodes.rationale: Navigation controls must allow viewing in first or third person via keyboard/mouse/joystick or a mix, and the user must interact with scene elements (moving objects or lights) that respond to input.

nodes.label: BRDF / shading models
nodes.rationale: Fragment shaders implement models such as Lambert or Oren-Nayar diffuse, Toon, Blinn/Phong/Ward specular, or Cook-Torrance with GGX or other distributions/geometric terms.

nodes.label: Direct and indirect lighting
nodes.rationale: Must use both direct lighting (directional, point, spotlights or custom) and indirect approximations such as ambient light or Image Based Lighting.

nodes.label: Material parameters and advanced textures
nodes.rationale: Material parameters (diffuse/specular color, emission, roughness, metalness) come from uniforms or textures; textures also drive advanced techniques like normal maps or detail textures.

nodes.label: Image quality and extra elements
nodes.rationale: Final image quality and project size count; extra elements like animation, basic physics simulation, algorithmic intelligence, on-screen display, start-up menus, splash screens and scene changes are positively evaluated.

nodes.label: Provided 3D assets (encouraged own)
nodes.rationale: An extensive asset set (food, furniture, cars, buildings, vegetation, dungeons, terrain, schools, hospital wards, textures, PBR materials, HDRI) is provided on WeBeep; using own/obtained assets is encouraged and positively evaluated.

nodes.label: Project registration form (Microsoft Form)
nodes.rationale: Each group registers via a Microsoft Form (link on WeBeep) specifying curriculum, teammates, topic and a short feature description; open until mid-January 2027, suggested at ~40% implementation; unregistered students cannot present.

nodes.label: Topic: Haunted Castle Explorer
nodes.rationale: Simplified 3D real-time exploration of a haunted castle; user navigates rooms and interacts (open secret passages, pick up objects, light candles, trigger hidden mechanisms).

nodes.label: Topic: Dungeon Tavern NPC
nodes.rationale: 3D tavern where the user in first person approaches virtual characters (innkeeper, bard, merchant) and triggers interaction by getting close and pressing a key.

nodes.label: Topic: Enchanted Forest Wanderer
nodes.rationale: Simplified 3D real-time exploration of an enchanted forest; navigate and interact (collect herbs, activate glowing plants, feed animals, unlock hidden paths).

nodes.label: Topic: Modular School Classroom Planner
nodes.rationale: Interactive 3D environment to build/arrange a classroom by placing modular elements (desks, chairs, blackboards, shelves) in a room, moving/rotating/deleting via keyboard and/or GUI.

nodes.label: Topic: Hospital Resource Mover
nodes.rationale: Simplified 3D hospital simulation where the user relocates beds, equipment and supplies between rooms to meet changing ward requirements, navigating first person and interacting via keyboard/GUI.

nodes.label: Topic: Tabletop Dice RPG Arena
nodes.rationale: 3D tabletop environment to roll dice, move tokens on a grid and interact with game elements on a virtual table; camera can rotate around the table and zoom to inspect the board.

nodes.label: Topic: Animal Herding Simulator
nodes.rationale: Third-person farming-management style simulator (Stardew Valley/Hay Day) where a character herds animals to marked areas within a time limit; animal movements need not be animated.

nodes.label: Topic: Vehicle Simulator
nodes.rationale: Third-person simulator controlling a vehicle (car, truck, airplane, drone, helicopter) performing precise movement to reach marked pads in a 3D environment.

nodes.label: Registration Microsoft Form link
nodes.rationale: Project registration is done via a Microsoft Forms link; the form can be compiled starting Monday, May 18th.

nodes.label: Individual project: motivation mandatory
nodes.rationale: For an individual project, motivation is mandatory; lack of it was a main past reason for rejected proposals.

nodes.label: Every member registers individually
nodes.rationale: For groups of 2-3, ALL members must submit their own form entry confirming the other members' names and the topic, so the professor can verify each member agrees.

nodes.label: MGCG proprietary asset format
nodes.rationale: Assets are stored in the mildly-encrypted proprietary .mgcg format, licensed ONLY for the CG final project (many bought from CGTrader); each thumbnail PNG helps pick objects; students must respect licensing and not reuse elsewhere.

nodes.label: Shared texture per asset folder
nodes.rationale: All assets in folder XXX share texture Textures/Textures_XXX.png (e.g. City/Apartment_1.mgcg and City/Box_001.mgcg use Textures/Textures_City.png).

nodes.label: skeleton2026 mandatory starting point
nodes.rationale: The _Code/skeleton2026.zip with the latest Starter.hpp (including MGCG model readers) MUST be used as the project base; existing projects should migrate assets/sources into it (backward compatible).

nodes.label: Cannot modify Starter.hpp / include folder
nodes.rationale: Students are not allowed to change Starter.hpp or any file in the include folder of the skeleton.

nodes.label: Professor Starter.hpp collects grading data
nodes.rationale: At delivery the project is recompiled with a 'professor' version of Starter.hpp that also collects information about the implementation used to determine the grade, which is why the starting point must be fixed.
